name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: The real fight happening in Texas
body:
There’s really only one true fight going on in Texas.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I recently had the chance to chat with Jon Favreau on Pod Save America, and I want to share a piece of that conversation because it gets to the absolute core of why I’m running for governor.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260702_1_pod.2TCe-d&refcode=em20260702-1478&amount=5&t=1&akid=1478%2E299639%2EK8QC-N)
During my time serving in the Texas House, I watched the political theater up close and personal, and it was messy. But it also taught me an important lesson: the real division in our state isn't what you see on the news. It isn’t Left vs. Right. Behind all the noise, there’s really only _one true fight_ going on in Texas.
**And that fight boils down to whether we’re going to be a state that is truly by and for the people,_or_ will we allow it to remain a world built exclusively for billionaires?**
Right now, the people are losing. While Abbott uses culture wars to divide us, our public schools are starved of resources, and everyday families can no longer afford the basics. It’s a deliberate strategy to keep us looking the wrong way while our government hands over our resources and our tax dollars to their wealthy donors on a silver platter.
**We have a chance to end this cycle and officially vote Greg Abbott out of office this fall.**
That’s why I’m running to be a governor who works for every single Texan — no matter their political party.
But to cut through the billionaire-funded distraction machine, I need a powerhouse grassroots team standing right beside me.
**[Will you donate $5 or whatever you can afford today to support my campaign and help us focus on the fight that actually matters?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260702_1_pod.2TCe-d&refcode=em20260702-1478&amount=5&t=2&akid=1478%2E299639%2EK8QC-N)**

Thank you,
Gina Hinojosa

| | Dear Friend,

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

**That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today.** It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected.

**You can take your quiz by using the secure link below:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/3BoAjLeqt0upHzeJxO218-fNNjsYcy58RMxEDKeqOumSPoPdB76QhC0_dFOmpwlnQXcy9BPponecGe0ysxQ0HhzZaNa_vzFAlW8bsCROJV56RsDN1jEAlNjkqhhl0wS491bC52V336Shf_T1QjQsgcEwyA_FSNsIB6WRxwF93DndMovcw0OBATBCZTkOFZxf0hGtDmLvhv4qfTKvLJGrAsurBm6xJbyjXt3WJw0zoVVDG-WJ7oAhn2sxSPO4-oWn0oVXFkMVvcocvKIbEryvmDzkfGiPSF9a8u_CxEAx8-im0yZprLEZyxzrQmMX7lvfahFiSo9zPnQUKuDzR4f4-d9SjWT4wpCAfa1Yz6nnlschr6hOt5ZX1FIShBvLNr_b5O-KyAiB6sjq9df9odKv1_M39-qprIjYv2bvdGFezworU7uXr3tvCnS6te0ZWexAI_EcnrzFD5qnvRYzGSCb09odwGLZDfTQuoOGE2pVZZtyiYEInSLB-PZTF9WgNiYlLPRXpqYX8c1yBaEcsPvCcWFpeAVfB3Z80LPSf1IWkCc1nJLUnDL4tCgrGT9tuPPjNnZxHQTtDT9iWXzGy-vuVgDrZ3bO4s_V4f2YYKvAmma4XopFsOoj6Rth21YSOoXAk1R0yEPaswD23w5Qk4GOc_LhGdpuMgyDij_arrI9eY3E3NUFQMYh0VLZns8ez2NhaUzvv71vM04RZ9UylKjQ9i0fBKvBXLbPQi3um11w2U1ImDIfNB43VCTMbo1SrEJhFrEpHAIsrAEjCKFNU5yH97_i8eYdj6NWe5MZhiMMO9UScSCm6LV1sVSete0oXwLyzQ/SiZ9ngmqGT-5uLN_-NW-T3wSyAF8b2vI/22)

For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government.

**But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection.**

The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty.

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, **reaching and teaching millions** of Americans in all 50 states.

When you take the **National Quiz on Presidential Selection** , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to **share this** information with your fellow Americans.

So please take your **National Quiz on Presidential Selection**. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

body:
Too many politicians have treated public office like an opportunity to enrich themselves.
#
Peter,
While working families across the country struggle to pay the bills, Washington keeps reminding us that the rules don’t apply to those at the top.
According to newly released financial disclosures, **Donald Trump’s investment accounts executed thousands of stock trades** through 2025 while he was making decisions that impacted financial markets.
In a recent interview with Aaron Parnas, Tim Walz said it best:
_“This idea that you would trade stocks on information that you have is insidious. It undermines faith in government, it cheats the system, it puts all of us at risk.”_
[__](https://act.timwalz.com/signup/em-20260702-ban-stock-trading/?t=2&akid=827%2E34582%2ElJw_T8)
[**If you agree with Tim, add your name to our petition calling for a ban on congressional and presidential stock trading NOW →**](https://act.timwalz.com/signup/em-20260702-ban-stock-trading/?t=3&akid=827%2E34582%2ElJw_T8)
The day before Trump announced a 90-day pause on his sweeping tariffs — a decision that sent the stock market soaring — his investment accounts purchased _hundreds_ of individual stocks near the market’s low point.
To make matters worse, those trades weren’t legally disclosed until over a year later, despite federal laws requiring government officials to disclose stock transactions within 45 days. As a result, he paid a measly $200 fine — a slap on the wrist.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/signup/em-20260702-ban-stock-trading/?t=4&akid=827%2E34582%2ElJw_T8)
Let’s face it: _this is the most corrupt presidential administration in our country’s history._
**Too many politicians — especially Trump — have treated public office like an opportunity to enrich themselves instead of serving the people who elected them.**
We don’t have to accept this, Peter.

body:
We’re not afraid to talk about war, about foreign policy, about what it means to fight for your country abroad and then come home to do the same thing.
#
Peter,
20 years ago, VoteVets started as a scrappy organization founded by a few pissed off Veterans who were ready to fight back against the Republican Party.
Today, it’s a nationwide organization composed of millions of Veterans, members of Military Families, professionals from intelligence and national security... and, frankly, a ton of regular people who understand what we’re trying to do here.
This isn’t your run-of-the-mill Democratic political shop. We’re not afraid to talk about war, about foreign policy, about what it means to fight for your country abroad and then come home to do the same thing. We go places most other organizations won’t, speak to people they can’t, and we win when nobody else can.
The flag belongs to all of us. Patriotism belongs to all of us. This country is ours, just as much as it is Donald Trump’s or any of his MAGA die-hards. And more than that, we actually believe in it. We believe in our democracy, our Constitution, our way of life — and we swore an oath to support and defend it.
That’s our mission, that’s what VoteVets is about and what sets us apart. And before America’s 250th July Fourth, we’re asking you to double down on your past support and recommit to our mission.
[**If you are with VoteVets, if you believe what we do matters, and you’re willing to stand with us in the fight for our country, add your name and personally endorse the VoteVets mission.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/260702_VV_mission_em?source=em260702-1-120&refcode2=35299.3013755.4awxPP&akid=35299%2E3013755%2E4awxPP)

subject: Our Weekly Newsletter Is Here!
body:
It's Been A Great Week On The Campaign Trail

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/elizabethforvirginia/our-weekly-newsletter-is-here-7hpfpb2621?e=2f83c585b2)

|
---
|

| | | | | |
# _Our Weekly Newsletter Is Here!_
---
| | **Hello everyone!****The summer heat has been in full force, but that hasn't slowed our campaign down!****The week kicked off at the Virginia Democrats Blue Commonwealth Gala, where Elizabeth was excited to spend time with supporters and share our vision for the future. She had the chance to connect with elected officials, candidates, and activists from across the Commonwealth who are working every day to move Virginia forward. The energy in the room was inspiring, and we’re grateful for everyone who took the time to talk about the campaign.****After the gala, Elizabeth joined the Virginia Young Democrats Afterparty, where she celebrated the incredible work being done by the next generation of leaders. It was exciting to meet so many passionate young people who are stepping up to serve their communities and shape the future of our country. ****On Sunday, Elizabeth was honored to speak at the Rural Democrats Brunch, where she had thoughtful conversations about the issues that matter most to rural Virginians. She discussed strengthening rural education, expanding access to quality healthcare, supporting our local economies, and ensuring every community has the resources it needs to thrive. ****Monday brought another meaningful opportunity as Elizabeth joined two fellow candidates for a Veterans Candidate Forum. As a veteran, Elizabeth knows that service doesn't end when you take off the uniform. She and the other candidates discussed how their military experiences have prepared them to lead, solve problems, and put people before politics. ****Weeks like this remind us that campaigns are powered by people. Whether you met Elizabeth at an event, stopped to chat in the heat, or you're following along from home, thank you for being part of this movement!**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Upcoming Events:****Come out and get involved this week! On Thursday, we will be hosting one of our**[**regular phonebanks.**](https://us.list-manage.com/Xs9gNNcgH2g?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** The following day, we’ll be hosting a **[**canvass in Glen Allen**](https://us.list-manage.com/Zn6TYsp41fZ?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**(fingers crossed that the weather holds.) ****On Saturday, it’s time to celebrate the 4th of July! Elizabeth will be out in the community all day. Stop by the**[**Hampton Park Parade**](https://us.list-manage.com/NfxpfWqtYyd?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** in the morning, and you might even have a chance to join us in the parade. That afternoon, we’ll be celebrating the holiday in **[**Historic Williamsburg.**](https://us.list-manage.com/whqSSjc1s7b?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**And finally, we’ll catch some**[**fireworks in Yorktown**](https://us.list-manage.com/JfVGhRQ4WEu?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**to close out the night.****On Sunday morning, join us for some fun and activism! We’ll be hosting a**[**postcarding and pool party**](https://us.list-manage.com/9Gjcsrsm7pP?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** event, so be sure to join us for some food, postcards, and swimming. That evening, join us for a **[**virtual phonebank**](https://us.list-manage.com/1B2tTajutdF?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)** or stop by and say hello at the **[**Hardywood Meet & Greet!**](https://us.list-manage.com/8CmZCZCblWV?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**Let’s have a great week, VA!**

Abdul is building a winning coalition by putting forward an agenda that speaks directly to working people. He is not afraid to take on the greed making life unaffordable across Michigan because he’s never taken a dime in corporate donations.
When he gets to Washington, he will work to get big money out of politics and to guarantee health care as a human right to all Americans.

|
Peter,
The Supreme Court issued one slightly reasonable ruling today and allowed mail-in ballots that are postmarked by Election Day to be counted after polls close, reaffirming the core power of states to administer elections.
In response, the President of the United States took to Truth Social, to say the very idea of free and fair elections are "more dangerous than World War I, World War II, Pearl Harbor, or September 11th"
He's now using the ruling as leverage to further pressure GOP Senators to nuke the filibuster and pass the mammoth SAVE Act voter suppression bill:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019Gk4doEUF4LibMwzdX7GOxkAuZBU4ib2XiL9_TOa9uk1coqOixbQ-LPlBTHqg9d5fqNSLZbotdJD_nW3CsxNmgYiQb81m8h-iQeetI3iY5sTx_27wbnmX10lEDsSOgxobI9UisDzKs5H1SPrA7PYidxBv9HJwKEVOVMChzS9bTw2fwy045gvUOLsit7O3rVH4wNS4hznKWyRXdOhAZvM-1wG16DcgL95iUvL7EYOY92VBqRGX3oWQA==&c=18g42ObDPW39YY0ps5s13v6U5tR1ZOxan6-IhvezqZHJIiweWRmsyw==&ch=7A7kGERUEfics70qqlMjpuynuEo2xexhAjNlMo4iHxF9tBqibki1vg==)
---
"Never forget the tragedy of 9/11" is apparently no longer something the Republican Party holds sacred.
The so-called "SAVE Act" is Trump's one and only legislative priority right now for a good reason: the bill is an unprecedented, massive voter suppression agenda that has no equal in modern American history.
Passing this bill would throw the midterm elections happening in just four short months into absolute chaos--exactly what Trump would need to declare an emergency and cancel any election results he doesn't like.
The stakes of our fight are astronomical. If states cannot hold the line against a head-on MAGA attack on the very foundation of free and fair elections, our democracy will cease to exist in November and only a twisted Trumpian nightmare will take its place.
Democrats cannot just cross their fingers and instruct the American people to "vote harder" while Trump brings the full might of the federal government down on the civil servants doing their jobs. We have to be on offense right now, not four months from now.
[Defend Our Courts is fighting to win critical state supreme court races to strengthen our last line of defense against the forthcoming MAGA assault on elections. But the firewall cannot hold if we don't put everything we have into this. Team, my friends over at Resist Reclaim Rebuild said I could reach out:
I'm honored to share that I have officially become the Democratic nominee for Congress in NY-21.
I am grateful for everyone who has believed that a dairy farmer from the North Country could build something strong enough to compete in one of the most important races in the country.
When we launched back in December of 2024, I didn't do it because I wanted to be a politician. I did it because I love this community, and I believe the people here deserve someone who knows their struggles, because they've lived them too.
Over the last year, I've traveled this district, met with families, listened to workers, farmers, parents, veterans, and small business owners.
Everywhere I went, I heard the same thing: people are tired of being forgotten.
That's what brought us here.
But this isn't the finish line. It's the beginning of the next chapter.
The eyes of the country are turning toward NY-21. More money will enter this race. More attention will follow. The fight ahead won't be easy.
But I've never been afraid of hard work.
On the farm, you don't stop working because you've finished one job. You get up the next morning and start the next one.
That's exactly what we're going to do.
Will you split a donation of $25—or whatever you can afford— between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor of our General Election campaign right now? Your early support is the fuel we need to build a winning infrastructure, hire organizers, and ensure our message reaches every corner of NY-21. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-blake]

name: Aria, United We Dream
subject: Our communities are stronger than these attacks
body:
Citizenship is the only lasting protection. We're calling on Congress to deliver it. | | | Peter, This country has relied on the labor, care, and contributions of our immigrant coworkers, neighbors, and loved ones for generations. Now, with the protections they've relied on diminishing, they face the threat of job loss, the stripping of legal protections, and family separation. From court rulings targeting Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders and asylum seekers to ongoing attacks on DACA and birthright citizenship, _the strategy is clear: strip millions of legal protections and narrow the definition of belonging in this country._ **That's what the largest delegalization effort in modern U.S. history looks like.** **[The fight to protect our communities from mass delegalization is urgent. Our organizing must match the moment. United We Dream relies on your support to fuel this advocacy. Will you chip in $10 today?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAe_ANaZPpDQuekprkyb6preo-SPVaonq8ZGZKS0mnIHz-yzp8VybRXcSnd8Bz6M9MlDoT69I6hHal0GeWh6XwvjFMr5EPeEGxPC56MVQhVlwMT2msd69MZ49CYcnGxHlhKwAlURyAe518T6FuiSqhCadAPJVcpiztvIfaKA_5oXHQm1i4l6hDf4g3XC7zuFZoX_9D5wyF23cJKtwM7qEi5C2XH98QoVNTSmiajXVwiR64MqiyVFVrXX2zcxfjra3lmVMXt8HfXZp45abUjqLszenATA6iTKzP4ivwp3IY4wUB8UHmTJHWm5XMSfzWahZ6j1zaBBNzs1L5KjS9X3B3XCVfKsamYdkDZk6QG_pqv7UkNkgiBPuwTvlwYaownB4Eg4AonbXDahZvFwcVb1p7ufKXtjlGzH62U-S6_dzFHI7kYUrf2o5watkc6qUPFTwpMK0Oaa1fICKtMLEivwguHbg/4rz/Il5wOmxdQ7mLJWoIAeAmZA/h0/h001.0W6_7nvvbMbuV6E4bsJd1Pgn-aBS2mzFxlzzZY_R4dA)** For months, this administration has escalated its attacks on legal immigration protections, targeting TPS, DACA, asylum, and other humanitarian programs that have helped families stay together and communities thrive. This isn't happening in isolation; it’s part of a broader campaign to redefine who is an American:
* **DACA:** Processing delays are causing status lapses, leaving thousands of recipients exposed to deportation, while the Justice Department makes it easier to detain and deport DACA recipients.1
* **TPS:** Termination for 14 of 17 countries puts over 1.3 million people at risk of detention or deportation, with consequences for 2.3 million U.S. citizens with loved ones who rely on TPS.2
* **Broad Attacks:** Refugee admissions are effectively halted, green card applicants face increasingly harsh reviews, and the Supreme Court is currently reviewing challenges to birthright citizenship.3

With every new court ruling and executive action, it becomes harder for millions of working people to safely remain in the United States. Congress must act swiftly to defend the rights of all working people and provide a pathway to citizenship. **[Home is here, and we aren't going anywhere. clean_body: Citizenship is the only lasting protection. We're calling on Congress to deliver it. | | | Peter, This country has relied on the labor, care, and contributions of our immigrant coworkers, neighbors, and loved ones for generations. Now, with the protections they've relied on diminishing, they face the threat of job loss, the stripping of legal protections, and family separation. From court rulings targeting Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders and asylum seekers to ongoing attacks on DACA and birthright citizenship, the strategy is clear: strip millions of legal protections and narrow the definition of belonging in this country. That's what the largest delegalization effort in modern U.S. history looks like. For months, this administration has escalated its attacks on legal immigration protections, targeting TPS, DACA, asylum, and other humanitarian programs that have helped families stay together and communities thrive. This isn't happening in isolation; it’s part of a broader campaign to redefine who is an American: DACA: Processing delays are causing status lapses, leaving thousands of recipients exposed to deportation, while the Justice Department makes it easier to detain and deport DACA recipients.1 TPS: Termination for 14 of 17 countries puts over 1.3 million people at risk of detention or deportation, with consequences for 2.3 million U.S. citizens with loved ones who rely on TPS.2 Broad Attacks: Refugee admissions are effectively halted, green card applicants face increasingly harsh reviews, and the Supreme Court is currently reviewing challenges to birthright citizenship.3 With every new court ruling and executive action, it becomes harder for millions of working people to safely remain in the United States. Congress must act swiftly to defend the rights of all working people and provide a pathway to citizenship. There’s something the Left never thought they’d have to say out loud:

_They’re losing the numbers game._

And now they’re fundraising in a panic because of it:

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S.-Iran Doha talks conclude; Pakistan says "positive progress" made: **Pakistan's Foreign Ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/af97bbde-d987-4abd-9fb3-54c8d2f6d32f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) indirect talks between Iranian and U.S. delegations in Doha concluded with "positive progress" on issues related to the implementation of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. In a statement on Thursday, the ministry said the parties agreed to continue discussions in the coming period, with the next round of talks to be scheduled "at the earliest possible time" following the funeral processions for the late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, which are scheduled from July 4 to 9.
* **Iran 's parliament speaker calls for mass turnout at Khamenei funeral: **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/c1114914-dc0b-4c9e-acf6-19051e099d32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iranians to attend the funeral ceremonies of the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in large numbers, urging the public to "write a glorious page in the history of Islamic Iran" through their participation, IRNA reported. In a statement ahead of the ceremonies, Ghalibaf said "the nation's call for vengeance must ring in the ears of the whole world." Khamenei, 86, was assassinated in Tehran on February 28, the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The funeral procession will take place across several significant locations, beginning in Tehran, the seat of state institutions, before continuing through Qom, the Iraqi holy cities of Karbala and Najaf, and concluding in Mashhad.
* **Ghalibaf denies IAEA access to bombed nuclear sites:** On Wednesday, Ghalibaf [called](https://substack.com/redirect/b886cdcc-712b-482c-8213-fd80d0efff5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reports that IAEA inspectors would be granted access to Iran's bombed nuclear sites "false," citing a law and resolution passed by parliament and the Supreme National Security Council governing inspections. He said IAEA inspectors are currently authorized to access only the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant and the Tehran Research Reactor, adding that "under no circumstances will access be granted to sites that have been bombed and damaged."
* **Trump administration reportedly urges Iran to drop shipping toll plans in favor of sanctions relief:** Washington is [telling](https://substack.com/redirect/44f7b914-79a9-4f08-b753-babeb5ce6fae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran to "think bigger" than shipping tolls, arguing a full sanctions-lifting deal tied to a broader nuclear agreement would be worth "100 times more" to the country, Axios reported on Wednesday.
* The U.S and Iranian teams met in Doha on Thursday, where the U.S. reportedly agreed to release the first $3 billion tranche for humanitarian purchases, according to Al Arabiya. U.S. officials denied any such deal.
* **Senior Iranian diplomat rejects CENTCOM-led security summit in Bahrain:** Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister for legal and international affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/e30b0c01-4e37-41b0-b70b-9a006c8e2508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a CENTCOM-led security summit in Bahrain on Wednesday, saying "Hormuz is defined under Iran's command, not CENTCOM," and arguing that a military summit "cannot establish legal order and security for the Persian Gulf."
* Gharibabadi argued that regional security could only come through "the end of interventions and the U.S. withdrawal from the area."
* CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper hosted defense officials from 12 nations Wednesday, in what marked the first time Syrian and Lebanese military leaders joined a U.S.-led regional defense conference.
* **U.S. official claims Hormuz oil flows have surpassed 10 million barrels daily:** A U.S. official [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/81e9d9d0-6290-45c3-971d-a3ee09b73a6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Bloomberg on Wednesday that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have surpassed 10 million barrels per day. The official credited the increase to U.S. military "support" for shipping in the region, and argued Tehran's ability to disrupt shipping is now limited to targeting individual vessels
* Marine traffic monitors have counted roughly 30 to 40 transits this week. Goldman Sachs in a research note estimates oil exports from the Persian Gulf, accounting for all bypass routes, have recovered to a 7-day moving average of 18.2 million barrels per day by late June.
* Also on Thursday, Bloomberg energy analyst Javier Blas [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/eac542b4-ebff-4cf9-b7c3-fe9f4be22a92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the UAE has become the first Gulf oil producer to restore exports to roughly pre-war levels. June exports from the country climbed to more than 95% of pre-war volumes, with some tanker trackers indicating they have already exceeded pre-war levels. UAE crude is also increasingly being shipped to Europe and the U.S., beyond its traditional Asian markets.
* **NYT: Saudi and U.S. officials repeatedly clashed during Iran War:** The long-standing alliance between the U.S. and Saudi Arabia was [strained](https://substack.com/redirect/e9d8d528-1edf-48f9-80c4-8491b42e6511?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during the war, according to a Wednesday report from the New York Times. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman initially pushed President Donald Trump to take a harder line against Iran during the conflict, the report said, but shifted to urging a ceasefire after Iran demonstrated it could disrupt the Strait of Hormuz and threaten Gulf states.
* A key flashpoint came when Saudi Arabia refused to let the U.S. use its airspace for "Project Freedom," a mission to escort commercial shipping through the strait, forcing Washington to abandon the operation within 48 hours.
* Bin Salman also declined a G7 invitation as a result of the war, the report claimed, as Riyadh has increasingly pursued its own diplomacy with Iran, China, and Pakistan.

# Lebanon
* **Killed and wounded:** At least 4,298 people have been killed, and 12,196 wounded, in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry, as the death toll continues to rise due to recovery efforts and deaths resulting from wounds sustained in earlier Israeli attacks.
* **Israeli army carries out demolitions and strikes across Nabatieh:** Israeli forces carried out a series of demolitions across southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate over the past two days, according to Lebanon's National News Agency, despite a ceasefire in place. On Thursday, the Israeli army [detonated](https://substack.com/redirect/f749fd86-c227-4cbc-9de0-dd111a3dd47f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several homes in the town of Haddatha, triggering powerful explosions that reverberated across neighboring towns in the Bint Jbeil district. An Israeli drone strike targeted Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, a municipality in the Nabatieh Governorate. Israeli forces also [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/e79ca731-b0c2-45c6-9cf7-13d0ac41b4f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) major demolition operations near the town of Rshaf and in Beit Yahoun on Wednesday.
* The mayor of Nabatieh al-Fawqa urged Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to intervene over Israel's "daily attacks" on the town since the ceasefire. In a [letter](https://substack.com/redirect/90d4659a-acc9-4bdb-8342-cfacde183025?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) released on Thursday, the mayor said Nabatieh al-Fawqa has been subjected to airstrikes and drone attacks, while more than 10 civilians have been killed. He stressed that the town lies outside the so-called "yellow line," is not occupied, and was not included in any framework reports. He called on the Lebanese leadership to issue a clear official position on the town's legal and security status, halt the repeated attacks, and ensure residents can return "safely and with dignity."
* **Israel continues attacks in Lebanon despite ceasefire:** Israeli forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/457cd4b2-73d2-4593-bfe6-fa049ebe5f3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demolitions, arson, and shelling across parts of southern Lebanon on Wednesday, according to journalist Hadi Hoteit.
* Hoteit reported demolitions and fires in the border villages of Markaba, Beit Yahoun, Tiri, and Haddatha, all in the Bint Jbeil district near the Israeli border.
* An Israeli drone strike also hit a parked car in the Al-Deir neighborhood of Nabatieh, about 12 miles north of the border, after quadcopters reportedly dropped grenades in the area.

# Palestine
* **1,000 days of genocide in Gaza:** According to Gaza's Government Media Office, the following figures mark 1,000 days since the start of Israel's war on Gaza:
* Human toll
* 73,066 Palestinians killed and 173,514 wounded.
* 55% of those killed were children, women or elderly people.
* 262 journalists and 556 aid workers were killed.
* 58,800 children have been orphaned, with only one parent or none left; more than 2,700 families were erased from the civil registry.
* Healthcare
* 1,700 medical workers killed, 38 hospitals damaged, destroyed, or put out of service, and 197 ambulances targeted.
* More than 2.1 million cases of infectious diseases have been recorded, and over 22,000 patients need treatment abroad but are unable to leave Gaza due to Israeli restrictions.
* Destruction and displacement
* More than 90% of Gaza has been destroyed, with 223,000 tonnes of explosives dropped.
* 410,000 homes and buildings have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable.
* Around 2 million people were forcibly displaced, with 350,000 families needing shelter.
* Economic losses
* Direct losses across 15 sectors are estimated at $80 billion.
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 12 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. Two bodies were also recovered from under the rubble.
* Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,059 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,429, while 788 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli attacks on Gaza continue Wednesday:** Israeli strikes [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c053a071-e0b2-4be1-9cbb-27974ce03417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three Palestinians and wounded others across Gaza on Wednesday, as Israeli forces continued their violations of the ceasefire with home demolitions, attacks on displacement tents, and indiscriminate shelling, Palestine Online reported.
* Among these attacks, Israeli aircraft struck a group of people in the Sheikh Radhwan neighborhood of Gaza City, killing two and wounding several others.
* The Palestinian Red Crescent said its crews evacuated two wounded people, one in critical condition, after an Israeli strike hit a group of civilians on Omar al-Mukhtar Street in central Gaza City.
* In the south, Israeli vehicles fired directly at displacement tents and homes in the Qizan Rashwan area south of Khan Younis. A Rafah resident also died of wounds he had sustained a year earlier.

* **Gaza officials say famine has returned:** Only 25% of the food needs of Gaza's population are [entering](https://substack.com/redirect/fb0c2f8a-5de0-4009-aae5-0f810294bcf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Strip through crossings, Gaza's Social Development Ministry said Wednesday.
* Deputy Minister Riyad al-Bitar attributed the crisis to severe aid restrictions, economic collapse, and Israeli control over commercial trucks; he said Israel allows just 120 to 150 aid and commercial trucks daily against the 600 agreed upon under the October ceasefire. .

* **Israeli army kills Palestinian footballer, Football Association reports:** Israeli forces [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/2fafb6b1-04b3-41dc-baba-c9ccef328996?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saleem Al-Ashqar, 32, a goalkeeper for Khadamat Khan Younis who also played for Al-Aqsa and Al-Musaddar clubs, on Monday in Al-Qarara, northeast of Khan Younis, according to the Palestinian Football Association, which said he was recently married and awaiting his first child.
* The association put the total number of Palestinian sports figures killed since the genocide began at 1,009, including 567 from football, and said it has filed a complaint with FIFA seeking Israel's expulsion.
* **11 Palestinians killed, 866 detained in Jerusalem during first half of 2026:** At least 11 Palestinians were killed in occupied East Jerusalem during the first half of 2026, including eight shot by Israeli forces and three killed by Israeli settlers, the Jerusalem Governorate [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/ac30094e-b5b0-4cfa-81de-cd9b4e7fe3d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday. The governorate said Israeli authorities imposed a near-total closure of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, the third holiest place for Muslims, from February 28 through the reporting period, preventing worshippers from entering amid an escalation of settler incursions. It also recorded 269 Israeli settler attacks, 866 Palestinian arrests, 288 demolitions and land-leveling operations--including 66 forced self-demolitions--and 89 settlement-related plans and projects, which it said were part of a systematic policy aimed at expanding settlements and forcibly displacing Palestinians from Jerusalem.
* **U.S. and Israel sign deal for permanent Jerusalem embassy on contested Palestinian land:** The United States and Israel [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/e4eee06c-03fe-4651-910f-22167ddd8621?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an agreement to build a permanent U.S. Embassy compound on the 13-acre Allenby Barracks site in southern Jerusalem under a 99-year lease at $1 per year, despite ownership claims by Palestinian families holding pre-1948 land deeds, Ahram Online reported. Speaking at the signing ceremony, U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee said Washington would "plant our flag" in Jerusalem, which he called the "eternal, indigenous, and forever capital of the Jewish people." The move consolidates the embassy relocation ordered by President Donald Trump in 2017, which contravenes the Oslo framework, as well as UN resolutions rejecting unilateral changes to the city's status, including Security Council Resolution 478, which declared Israel's claim to a "complete and united" Jerusalem "null and void" and urged states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city.

* **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorses Abdul El-Sayed for Michigan Senate seat:** Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/83eff2ff-1171-45b0-a547-d32a06c1e58a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Dr. **Abdul El-Sayed** for Senate in Michigan in an interview with The New York Times, marking her first contested Senate primary endorsement of 2026 and putting her at odds with Senator **Chuck Schumer** , who backs the more moderate Representative Haley Stevens.

* **Melat Kiros says Hakeem Jeffries should not be House Speaker: Melat Kiros** , the democratic socialist who unseated 30-year-incumbent **Diana DeGette** in Colorado, told Politico on Wednesday that House Minority Leader **Hakeem Jeffries** should not become speaker if Democrats retake the House, arguing the party must "root out the corruption and get money out of our politics" by voting out incumbents who take corporate PAC money.
* Kiros later told CNN she would not vote for any Democrat for a leadership position who takes corporate PAC money.
* The candidate, who is presumed to win in November, also insisted to Axios that she would take a hard line on a number of the issues that [defined](https://substack.com/redirect/a63f74b8-7b69-468a-99b3-6b483accf44d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) her campaign. "If you want our votes on leadership, on appropriations, this is what it costs." A full embargo, she told Colorado Public Radio, "is the opinion of the vast majority of Democratic voters."
* Jeffries publicly congratulated Kiros on her primary win on Wednesday, calling it "hard-fought" and saying House Democrats would "end the culture of corruption in Washington."

* **Platner criticizes "legalized corruption":** Maine Democratic Senate candidate **Graham Platner** [called](https://substack.com/redirect/eeff4955-b09a-489e-8c44-c6c045e9d319?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) congressional stock ownership "legalized corruption" on Wednesday, saying lawmakers and their spouses should be barred from owning and trading individual stocks because they can profit from legislation they help pass.
* Sen. **Susan Collins 's** household stake in UnitedHealth Group is up 850%, Drop Site contributor Nathan Bernard noted on Wednesday, with the increase coming after Medicaid cuts in Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill" boosted the insurer's outlook.
* **ICE detains more than 10,000 people in five days:** Federal immigration officials [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/333046cd-0c2d-496e-bd7f-a540229e0a29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over 10,000 people in the last five days, according to documents obtained by The New York Times, after agency leaders ordered top ICE officials to focus more officers on arrests, with three officials saying the White House set a new standard of 2,000 arrests a day.
* Arrests peaked Saturday at more than 2,400, and the ICE detention population has risen to over 63,000 as of Tuesday.
* **OpenAI reportedly in early talks to give U.S. government 5% equity stake:** OpenAI is in early-stage, conceptual talks to give the U.S. government a 5% stake in the company, the Financial Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/759f53e1-faad-4ec1-a9ee-482d13a0a68e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, with CEO **Sam Altman** arguing this is the best way to share AI's benefits with the public.
* Altman has suggested that OpenAI and other major AI firms, including Anthropic, Google, and Meta, give 5% equity to a fund modeled on the Alaska Permanent Fund.
* Any deal could require an act of Congress, and Altman has reportedly discussed public ownership with President Donald Trump, Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** , Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** , and Senator **Bernie Sanders** , who has proposed a sovereign wealth fund financed by a one-time 50% tax on major AI companies' stock.
* **Presbyterian Church (USA) votes to recognize Gaza genocide, back arms embargo and divestment from Israel** : The General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church (USA), which represents the U.S.'s largest Presbyterian denomination, [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/247d3ab1-c390-40d7-a0ef-d70dc6d82e20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 454-15 Tuesday to adopt a resolution identifying Israel's war on Gaza as a genocide, lobby Congress for an arms embargo, and encourage members to boycott Israeli products tied to the war, following a separate 447-21 vote affirming the Kairos Palestine II statement calling for intensified boycott, divestment and sanctions efforts.
* A ranking member of the Church said that the Assembly had spoken "in a unified voice" against genocide and was similarly unified about "measures that will hopefully contribute to the liberation of Palestine."
* The votes came after the church on Sunday unanimously voted to divest from Palantir and GE Aerospace, adding to earlier divestments from HP, Motorola, Caterpillar, and Israeli bonds, and after its 2022 declaration that Israel is an apartheid state.

# Other International News
* **Syrian government says it is open to meeting Hezbollah** : Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3c337c0d-ee38-4715-a4f8-53b699687785?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during an official visit to Beirut that Damascus would be open to meeting Hezbollah "if interests require it," according to Lebanese state media. The visit--Shibani's first to Lebanon--comes after President Donald Trump suggested that Syria's new government could help combat Hezbollah, an offer Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has rejected in public statements.
* During the visit, Lebanon and Syria signed an agreement establishing a high-level cooperation committee, while Shibani said Damascus sought to overcome the "painful legacy" of relations between the two countries.
* **Bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills five** : A bomb planted inside a cafe in central Damascus [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/4162a1e5-14c0-49e4-8d28-cc25567330c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least five people and wounded 16, Syrian authorities said. The explosion took place near the Palace of Justice, a key government building, and shut down traffic throughout the center of the city. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
* **Over 900 arrested during South Africa anti-migrant protests** : South African police [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/a0cba6ec-7075-43d8-b926-03fb503df709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 900 people during nationwide anti-migrant demonstrations. In a statement, President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged public concerns over illegal immigration, border management, and pressure on services, but warned that "taking the law into one's own hands is vigilantism."
* Police said 120 marches took place across the country, with reports of looting and at least one person shot dead by police during a march in Johannesburg.
* **Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least 21** : A major Russian missile and drone barrage on Kyiv [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c02bd774-c03e-4b98-968e-1ab4ad053a51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 21 people and wounded dozens more, Ukrainian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy cut short a visit to Ireland and warned that Moscow was preparing a "massive" strike.
* Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said part of an apartment building collapsed after a direct hit, while city officials reported damage across dozens of locations and at least 90 people wounded with many more feared trapped under the rubble.
* Russia's Defense Ministry claimed that it targeted military and energy facilities around Kyiv and other regions in the overnight attacks which they also described as retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure.
* **Germany charges Ukrainian suspect over Nord Stream sabotage:** German federal prosecutors [indicted](https://substack.com/redirect/3027a16f-4af6-4b37-aa19-ee54290f7ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 50-year-old Ukrainian man identified as Serhii K over the 2022 explosions that destroyed the Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipelines linking Russia to Europe.
* Prosecutors allege he helped coordinate a team that used a sailing yacht to plant explosives near Denmark's Bornholm Island, serving as the operation's on-board coordinator rather than as a diver or bomb expert.
* Serhii K, previously identified as Serhii Kuznietsov after his 2025 arrest in Italy and extradition to Germany, has denied involvement and says he was serving in Ukraine's armed forces at the time, while the Ukrainian government has also continued to deny involvement in the attack which severed a critical export corridor for Russian natural gas.

* **Separatist Papua rebels claim to kill American pilot, burn plane in warning to U.S. and Indonesia:** Separatist fighters in Indonesia's Papua region, who have been waging a long-running insurgency against Jakarta, said they [shot dead](https://substack.com/redirect/e6e34526-d037-4a2c-bc2b-83802813a5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an American pilot, Nicholas F. Gosselin, and burned his aircraft after it landed in Yahukimo, accusing the civilian plane of repeatedly transporting Indonesian military personnel into rebel-declared "red zones."
* A spokesperson for the West Papua National Liberation Army said the attack was a message to Washington and Jakarta to cease working to suppress the separatist movement, which is seeking independence from Indonesia for the resource-rich western half of Papua.
* Indonesian police-military officials confirmed a burned plane carrying one American pilot and seven Papuan passengers was found at a local airport, though they said they could not yet verify whether rebels attacked it or whether the pilot was killed.
* **CPJ declines to exclude Palestinian and Lebanese journalists, keeps existing definition of "journalist": **The Committee to Protect Journalists' board [said](https://substack.com/redirect/616cffbe-a0ed-4f5e-b921-a3b331d3d4c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it voted Wednesday to affirm its existing definition of "who is a journalist," saying it never planned to narrow the definition to exclude Palestinian and Lebanese journalists killed by Israel, despite earlier reports suggesting the organization would consider removing that designation from journalists who work for "state-backed propaganda outlets, militant- and designated terror-affiliated organizations." The change was reportedly pushed by a right-wing outlet, The Washington Free Beacon.
* Former board member and Drop Site News publisher **Nika Soon-Shiong** had demanded a vote in an email to the board before her removal this week. "Reopening the question of 'who is a journalist' carries profound implications," Soon-Shiong said, adding that CPJ's database "should remain insulated from political pressure to redefine who deserves recognition for their role in history."

* **War-torn Sudan hit by deadly cholera outbreak:** At least 838 suspected cholera cases and 117 deaths have been [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f5e47792-d08c-409f-8c3f-0e3dd17ed975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Sudan's West Kordofan province, as the country's civil war continues to cripple healthcare and humanitarian access.
* World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed the outbreak, citing data from Sudan's Ministry of Health. He said the conflict has severely disrupted medical services and displaced communities, worsening the spread of the disease.
* Tedros added that fighting and roadblocks are hindering the delivery of humanitarian aid and preventing medical teams from reaching affected areas.

Iran and Ceasefire U.S.-Iran Doha talks conclude; Pakistan says "positive progress" made: Pakistan's Foreign Ministry indirect talks between Iranian and U.S. delegations in Doha concluded with "positive progress" on issues related to the implementation of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. In a statement on Thursday, the ministry said the parties agreed to continue discussions in the coming period, with the next round of talks to be scheduled "at the earliest possible time" following the funeral processions for the late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, which are scheduled from July 4 to 9. Iran 's parliament speaker calls for mass turnout at Khamenei funeral: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf Iranians to attend the funeral ceremonies of the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in large numbers, urging the public to "write a glorious page in the history of Islamic Iran" through their participation, IRNA reported. In a statement ahead of the ceremonies, Ghalibaf said "the nation's call for vengeance must ring in the ears of the whole world." Khamenei, 86, was assassinated in Tehran on February 28, the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The funeral procession will take place across several significant locations, beginning in Tehran, the seat of state institutions, before continuing through Qom, the Iraqi holy cities of Karbala and Najaf, and concluding in Mashhad. Ghalibaf denies IAEA access to bombed nuclear sites: On Wednesday, Ghalibaf reports that IAEA inspectors would be granted access to Iran's bombed nuclear sites "false," citing a law and resolution passed by parliament and the Supreme National Security Council governing inspections. He said IAEA inspectors are currently authorized to access only the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant and the Tehran Research Reactor, adding that "under no circumstances will access be granted to sites that have been bombed and damaged." Trump administration reportedly urges Iran to drop shipping toll plans in favor of sanctions relief: Washington is Iran to "think bigger" than shipping tolls, arguing a full sanctions-lifting deal tied to a broader nuclear agreement would be worth "100 times more" to the country, Axios reported on Wednesday. The U.S and Iranian teams met in Doha on Thursday, where the U.S. reportedly agreed to release the first $3 billion tranche for humanitarian purchases, according to Al Arabiya. U.S. officials denied any such deal. Senior Iranian diplomat rejects CENTCOM-led security summit in Bahrain: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister for legal and international affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, a CENTCOM-led security summit in Bahrain on Wednesday, saying "Hormuz is defined under Iran's command, not CENTCOM," and arguing that a military summit "cannot establish legal order and security for the Persian Gulf." Gharibabadi argued that regional security could only come through "the end of interventions and the U.S. withdrawal from the area." CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper hosted defense officials from 12 nations Wednesday, in what marked the first time Syrian and Lebanese military leaders joined a U.S.-led regional defense conference. U.S. official claims Hormuz oil flows have surpassed 10 million barrels daily: A U.S. official to Bloomberg on Wednesday that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have surpassed 10 million barrels per day. The official credited the increase to U.S. military "support" for shipping in the region, and argued Tehran's ability to disrupt shipping is now limited to targeting individual vessels Marine traffic monitors have counted roughly 30 to 40 transits this week. Goldman Sachs in a research note estimates oil exports from the Persian Gulf, accounting for all bypass routes, have recovered to a 7-day moving average of 18.2 million barrels per day by late June. Also on Thursday, Bloomberg energy analyst Javier Blas that the UAE has become the first Gulf oil producer to restore exports to roughly pre-war levels. June exports from the country climbed to more than 95% of pre-war volumes, with some tanker trackers indicating they have already exceeded pre-war levels. UAE crude is also increasingly being shipped to Europe and the U.S., beyond its traditional Asian markets. NYT: Saudi and U.S. officials repeatedly clashed during Iran War: The long-standing alliance between the U.S. and Saudi Arabia was during the war, according to a Wednesday report from the New York Times. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman initially pushed President Donald Trump to take a harder line against Iran during the conflict, the report said, but shifted to urging a ceasefire after Iran demonstrated it could disrupt the Strait of Hormuz and threaten Gulf states. A key flashpoint came when Saudi Arabia refused to let the U.S. use its airspace for "Project Freedom," a mission to escort commercial shipping through the strait, forcing Washington to abandon the operation within 48 hours. Bin Salman also declined a G7 invitation as a result of the war, the report claimed, as Riyadh has increasingly pursued its own diplomacy with Iran, China, and Pakistan. Lebanon Killed and wounded: At least 4,298 people have been killed, and 12,196 wounded, in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry, as the death toll continues to rise due to recovery efforts and deaths resulting from wounds sustained in earlier Israeli attacks. Israeli army carries out demolitions and strikes across Nabatieh: Israeli forces carried out a series of demolitions across southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate over the past two days, according to Lebanon's National News Agency, despite a ceasefire in place. On Thursday, the Israeli army several homes in the town of Haddatha, triggering powerful explosions that reverberated across neighboring towns in the Bint Jbeil district. An Israeli drone strike targeted Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, a municipality in the Nabatieh Governorate. Israeli forces also major demolition operations near the town of Rshaf and in Beit Yahoun on Wednesday. The mayor of Nabatieh al-Fawqa urged Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to intervene over Israel's "daily attacks" on the town since the ceasefire. In a released on Thursday, the mayor said Nabatieh al-Fawqa has been subjected to airstrikes and drone attacks, while more than 10 civilians have been killed. He stressed that the town lies outside the so-called "yellow line," is not occupied, and was not included in any framework reports. He called on the Lebanese leadership to issue a clear official position on the town's legal and security status, halt the repeated attacks, and ensure residents can return "safely and with dignity." Israel continues attacks in Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli forces demolitions, arson, and shelling across parts of southern Lebanon on Wednesday, according to journalist Hadi Hoteit. Hoteit reported demolitions and fires in the border villages of Markaba, Beit Yahoun, Tiri, and Haddatha, all in the Bint Jbeil district near the Israeli border. An Israeli drone strike also hit a parked car in the Al-Deir neighborhood of Nabatieh, about 12 miles north of the border, after quadcopters reportedly dropped grenades in the area. Palestine 1,000 days of genocide in Gaza: According to Gaza's Government Media Office, the following figures mark 1,000 days since the start of Israel's war on Gaza: Human toll 73,066 Palestinians killed and 173,514 wounded. 55% of those killed were children, women or elderly people. 262 journalists and 556 aid workers were killed. 58,800 children have been orphaned, with only one parent or none left; more than 2,700 families were erased from the civil registry. Healthcare 1,700 medical workers killed, 38 hospitals damaged, destroyed, or put out of service, and 197 ambulances targeted. More than 2.1 million cases of infectious diseases have been recorded, and over 22,000 patients need treatment abroad but are unable to leave Gaza due to Israeli restrictions. Destruction and displacement More than 90% of Gaza has been destroyed, with 223,000 tonnes of explosives dropped. 410,000 homes and buildings have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable. Around 2 million people were forcibly displaced, with 350,000 families needing shelter. Economic losses Direct losses across 15 sectors are estimated at $80 billion. Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 12 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. Two bodies were also recovered from under the rubble. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,059 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,429, while 788 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks on Gaza continue Wednesday: Israeli strikes three Palestinians and wounded others across Gaza on Wednesday, as Israeli forces continued their violations of the ceasefire with home demolitions, attacks on displacement tents, and indiscriminate shelling, Palestine Online reported. Among these attacks, Israeli aircraft struck a group of people in the Sheikh Radhwan neighborhood of Gaza City, killing two and wounding several others. The Palestinian Red Crescent said its crews evacuated two wounded people, one in critical condition, after an Israeli strike hit a group of civilians on Omar al-Mukhtar Street in central Gaza City. In the south, Israeli vehicles fired directly at displacement tents and homes in the Qizan Rashwan area south of Khan Younis. A Rafah resident also died of wounds he had sustained a year earlier. Gaza officials say famine has returned: Only 25% of the food needs of Gaza's population are the Strip through crossings, Gaza's Social Development Ministry said Wednesday. Deputy Minister Riyad al-Bitar attributed the crisis to severe aid restrictions, economic collapse, and Israeli control over commercial trucks; he said Israel allows just 120 to 150 aid and commercial trucks daily against the 600 agreed upon under the October ceasefire. . Israeli army kills Palestinian footballer, Football Association reports: Israeli forces Saleem Al-Ashqar, 32, a goalkeeper for Khadamat Khan Younis who also played for Al-Aqsa and Al-Musaddar clubs, on Monday in Al-Qarara, northeast of Khan Younis, according to the Palestinian Football Association, which said he was recently married and awaiting his first child. The association put the total number of Palestinian sports figures killed since the genocide began at 1,009, including 567 from football, and said it has filed a complaint with FIFA seeking Israel's expulsion. 11 Palestinians killed, 866 detained in Jerusalem during first half of 2026: At least 11 Palestinians were killed in occupied East Jerusalem during the first half of 2026, including eight shot by Israeli forces and three killed by Israeli settlers, the Jerusalem Governorate on Thursday. The governorate said Israeli authorities imposed a near-total closure of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, the third holiest place for Muslims, from February 28 through the reporting period, preventing worshippers from entering amid an escalation of settler incursions. It also recorded 269 Israeli settler attacks, 866 Palestinian arrests, 288 demolitions and land-leveling operations--including 66 forced self-demolitions--and 89 settlement-related plans and projects, which it said were part of a systematic policy aimed at expanding settlements and forcibly displacing Palestinians from Jerusalem. U.S. and Israel sign deal for permanent Jerusalem embassy on contested Palestinian land: The United States and Israel an agreement to build a permanent U.S. Embassy compound on the 13-acre Allenby Barracks site in southern Jerusalem under a 99-year lease at $1 per year, despite ownership claims by Palestinian families holding pre-1948 land deeds, Ahram Online reported. Speaking at the signing ceremony, U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee said Washington would "plant our flag" in Jerusalem, which he called the "eternal, indigenous, and forever capital of the Jewish people." The move consolidates the embassy relocation ordered by President Donald Trump in 2017, which contravenes the Oslo framework, as well as UN resolutions rejecting unilateral changes to the city's status, including Security Council Resolution 478, which declared Israel's claim to a "complete and united" Jerusalem "null and void" and urged states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorses Abdul El-Sayed for Michigan Senate seat: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for Senate in Michigan in an interview with The New York Times, marking her first contested Senate primary endorsement of 2026 and putting her at odds with Senator Chuck Schumer , who backs the more moderate Representative Haley Stevens. Ocasio-Cortez has not yet endorsed Graham Platner in his Maine Senate campaign, nor did she endorse the primary campaigns of Darializa Avila Chevalier , Clare Valdez , or Brad Lander , who, after their recent victories, will join her in New York's congressional delegation. Melat Kiros says Hakeem Jeffries should not be House Speaker: Melat Kiros , the democratic socialist who unseated 30-year-incumbent Diana DeGette in Colorado, told Politico on Wednesday that House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries should not become speaker if Democrats retake the House, arguing the party must "root out the corruption and get money out of our politics" by voting out incumbents who take corporate PAC money. Kiros later told CNN she would not vote for any Democrat for a leadership position who takes corporate PAC money. The candidate, who is presumed to win in November, also insisted to Axios that she would take a hard line on a number of the issues that her campaign. "If enough of us share that commitment to Medicare for All, to ending corporate capture, to an arms embargo, we should absolutely say: here are our conditions," she told the outlet. "If you want our votes on leadership, on appropriations, this is what it costs." A full embargo, she told Colorado Public Radio, "is the opinion of the vast majority of Democratic voters." Jeffries publicly congratulated Kiros on her primary win on Wednesday, calling it "hard-fought" and saying House Democrats would "end the culture of corruption in Washington." Platner criticizes "legalized corruption": Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner congressional stock ownership "legalized corruption" on Wednesday, saying lawmakers and their spouses should be barred from owning and trading individual stocks because they can profit from legislation they help pass. Sen. Susan Collins 's household stake in UnitedHealth Group is up 850%, Drop Site contributor Nathan Bernard noted on Wednesday, with the increase coming after Medicaid cuts in Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill" boosted the insurer's outlook. ICE detains more than 10,000 people in five days: Federal immigration officials over 10,000 people in the last five days, according to documents obtained by The New York Times, after agency leaders ordered top ICE officials to focus more officers on arrests, with three officials saying the White House set a new standard of 2,000 arrests a day. Arrests peaked Saturday at more than 2,400, and the ICE detention population has risen to over 63,000 as of Tuesday. OpenAI reportedly in early talks to give U.S. government 5% equity stake: OpenAI is in early-stage, conceptual talks to give the U.S. government a 5% stake in the company, the Financial Times on Thursday, with CEO Sam Altman arguing this is the best way to share AI's benefits with the public. Altman has suggested that OpenAI and other major AI firms, including Anthropic, Google, and Meta, give 5% equity to a fund modeled on the Alaska Permanent Fund. Any deal could require an act of Congress, and Altman has reportedly discussed public ownership with President Donald Trump, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent , and Senator Bernie Sanders , who has proposed a sovereign wealth fund financed by a one-time 50% tax on major AI companies' stock. Presbyterian Church (USA) votes to recognize Gaza genocide, back arms embargo and divestment from Israel : The General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church (USA), which represents the U.S.'s largest Presbyterian denomination, 454-15 Tuesday to adopt a resolution identifying Israel's war on Gaza as a genocide, lobby Congress for an arms embargo, and encourage members to boycott Israeli products tied to the war, following a separate 447-21 vote affirming the Kairos Palestine II statement calling for intensified boycott, divestment and sanctions efforts. A ranking member of the Church said that the Assembly had spoken "in a unified voice" against genocide and was similarly unified about "measures that will hopefully contribute to the liberation of Palestine." The votes came after the church on Sunday unanimously voted to divest from Palantir and GE Aerospace, adding to earlier divestments from HP, Motorola, Caterpillar, and Israeli bonds, and after its 2022 declaration that Israel is an apartheid state. Other International News Syrian government says it is open to meeting Hezbollah : Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani during an official visit to Beirut that Damascus would be open to meeting Hezbollah "if interests require it," according to Lebanese state media. The visit--Shibani's first to Lebanon--comes after President Donald Trump suggested that Syria's new government could help combat Hezbollah, an offer Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has rejected in public statements. During the visit, Lebanon and Syria signed an agreement establishing a high-level cooperation committee, while Shibani said Damascus sought to overcome the "painful legacy" of relations between the two countries. Bomb blast at Damascus cafe kills five : A bomb planted inside a cafe in central Damascus at least five people and wounded 16, Syrian authorities said. The explosion took place near the Palace of Justice, a key government building, and shut down traffic throughout the center of the city. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Over 900 arrested during South Africa anti-migrant protests : South African police more than 900 people during nationwide anti-migrant demonstrations. In a statement, President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged public concerns over illegal immigration, border management, and pressure on services, but warned that "taking the law into one's own hands is vigilantism." Police said 120 marches took place across the country, with reports of looting and at least one person shot dead by police during a march in Johannesburg. Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least 21 : A major Russian missile and drone barrage on Kyiv at least 21 people and wounded dozens more, Ukrainian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy cut short a visit to Ireland and warned that Moscow was preparing a "massive" strike. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said part of an apartment building collapsed after a direct hit, while city officials reported damage across dozens of locations and at least 90 people wounded with many more feared trapped under the rubble. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed that it targeted military and energy facilities around Kyiv and other regions in the overnight attacks which they also described as retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil and gas infrastructure. Germany charges Ukrainian suspect over Nord Stream sabotage: German federal prosecutors a 50-year-old Ukrainian man identified as Serhii K over the 2022 explosions that destroyed the Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipelines linking Russia to Europe. Prosecutors allege he helped coordinate a team that used a sailing yacht to plant explosives near Denmark's Bornholm Island, serving as the operation's on-board coordinator rather than as a diver or bomb expert. Serhii K, previously identified as Serhii Kuznietsov after his 2025 arrest in Italy and extradition to Germany, has denied involvement and says he was serving in Ukraine's armed forces at the time, while the Ukrainian government has also continued to deny involvement in the attack which severed a critical export corridor for Russian natural gas. Separatist Papua rebels claim to kill American pilot, burn plane in warning to U.S. and Indonesia: Separatist fighters in Indonesia's Papua region, who have been waging a long-running insurgency against Jakarta, said they an American pilot, Nicholas F. Gosselin, and burned his aircraft after it landed in Yahukimo, accusing the civilian plane of repeatedly transporting Indonesian military personnel into rebel-declared "red zones." A spokesperson for the West Papua National Liberation Army said the attack was a message to Washington and Jakarta to cease working to suppress the separatist movement, which is seeking independence from Indonesia for the resource-rich western half of Papua. Indonesian police-military officials confirmed a burned plane carrying one American pilot and seven Papuan passengers was found at a local airport, though they said they could not yet verify whether rebels attacked it or whether the pilot was killed. CPJ declines to exclude Palestinian and Lebanese journalists, keeps existing definition of "journalist": The Committee to Protect Journalists' board it voted Wednesday to affirm its existing definition of "who is a journalist," saying it never planned to narrow the definition to exclude Palestinian and Lebanese journalists killed by Israel, despite earlier reports suggesting the organization would consider removing that designation from journalists who work for "state-backed propaganda outlets, militant- and designated terror-affiliated organizations." The change was reportedly pushed by a right-wing outlet, The Washington Free Beacon. Former board member and Drop Site News publisher Nika Soon-Shiong had demanded a vote in an email to the board before her removal this week. "Reopening the question of 'who is a journalist' carries profound implications," Soon-Shiong said, adding that CPJ's database "should remain insulated from political pressure to redefine who deserves recognition for their role in history." War-torn Sudan hit by deadly cholera outbreak: At least 838 suspected cholera cases and 117 deaths have been in Sudan's West Kordofan province, as the country's civil war continues to cripple healthcare and humanitarian access. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed the outbreak, citing data from Sudan's Ministry of Health. He said the conflict has severely disrupted medical services and displaced communities, worsening the spread of the disease. Tedros added that fighting and roadblocks are hindering the delivery of humanitarian aid and preventing medical teams from reaching affected areas. Derek,
250 years ago today — yes, July 2 , 1776 — thirteen colonies voted to formally declare independence from Great Britain. John Adams predicted the day would live on in fame forever.
Two days later, the text of the Declaration of Independence was officially adopted and ordered to be printed for wide distribution, setting in motion this great experiment of seeking a more perfect union and giving us an annual 4th of July holiday we have celebrated ever since. (The power of the press!)
A decade or so into our nation’s existence, after spending four months drafting our United States Constitution, Benjamin Franklin famously called our new government “ a republic, if you can keep it. ”
Now, we find ourselves celebrating America’s 250th birthday while in the midst of an ongoing fight to keep that republic formed two and a half centuries ago.
From the right to vote to the rule of law, the foundational promises of our country are being tested. We face immense challenges, led by a wannabe dictator who has threatened our fragile democracy more times than we can count, governed with chaos and cruelty, and started us down a slippery slope to authoritarianism.
As we mark this momentous Independence Day, I’m reflecting on the most optimistic values America was founded on: freedom, democracy, justice, equality, and love of country. I’m thinking about what it means to live in a free and fair democracy, and the responsibility we all share to protect it.
I’m also remembering that when our founders declared their own freedom from tyranny 250 years ago, not all in America were free. We're still working towards that North Star of true equality in our country, and it has never been more important to keep that work going.
It can be easy to feel dismayed, afraid, and angry at the trials we are navigating, collectively and individually. At the same time, as my mom Kathy taught me long ago: If you want to “be” right, be a pessimist. If you want to “do” right, be an optimist — and I determinedly remain so.
I still believe deeply in the American spirit. I believe in the power of the people to come together despite our differences, and to put in the work to shape a better future for the next 250 years.
I hope you’re able to spend this holiday weekend with loved ones and take time to celebrate the values that have always defined our country at its best.
Wishing you a happy 2nd of July, an early happy 4th of July, and wishing America a happy 250th birthday. Together, we will keep our republic!
Tim Kaine
U.S. Senator for Virginia
